interpretation: No root cause for the Android DNS behavior is proved; no operating-system workaround is shipped.

As-run reports using probe_escape for a shared HTTPS/DoT destination do not identify the originating UID. Their failure status and packet counts are retained. Current runner classification preserves the finding with origin_not_assumed.
Marked raw or fresh probe DNS payloads provide workload evidence separately from transport endpoint matching.

Physical gateway capture is whole-phone IPv4 traffic, not per-UID or per-profile attribution. Existing work-profile policy is only a possible source. The historical six DNS queries and original DoT SYN remain unassigned.
The new images are SDK Google APIs emulators with recorded module versions, not evidence about every current stock Android device or OTA/module combination.
No native IPv6 positive control succeeded. Cellular functional recovery does not establish cellular privacy without an upstream capture. Pixel-handoff report is nonexistent/missing.
Induced allocation pressure did not produce a Wave low-memory exit record. No natural LMK recovery or overnight reliability pass is claimed.
The direct-boot test uses a dedicated emulator and ordinary directBootAware helper. Credential removal was used for cleanup; it is not ordinary PIN-unlock or physical Pixel pre-unlock coverage.
The first split-tunnel automation could not observe checkbox state; no selection or bypass/inclusion success may be inferred from those failed attempts.

Manual split first bypass had an invalid setup because of an expired UI reference before the checkpoint advanced; the repeat bypass pass verified blocking policy and shared capture infrastructure with pixel-manual-split.
Manual split included-app observation was interrupted when ADB vanished; latest pixel-manual-split cleanup remains pending with ADB unavailable (parent handling cleanup separately).
